purpose: Evidence-backed expansion layer for the Potato of Life framework. It does not turn symbolic correspondences into facts; it places real historical, archaeological, botanical, anatomical and textual information beside the project's mythology so the relationships can be investigated precisely.
method: Each entry separates established evidence, historical interpretation and Potatoism correspondence.

layers.title: The real potato
facts: The potato was domesticated in the Andes by Indigenous peoples thousands of years ago.
Andean communities developed many varieties adapted to different elevations and environments.
Traditional preservation methods include chuño, using repeated freezing and drying.
After Spanish conquest the potato spread into Europe and became a major staple in parts of Europe by the eighteenth century.
layers.potatoism_reading: The real history makes the Potato metaphor unusually rich: an underground organ becomes a source of food, survives difficult environments, travels between civilizations and becomes part of radically different societies.
sources: Smithsonian Magazine, A Brief History of the Potato
Smithsonian Magazine, How the Potato Changed the World

layers.title: Tree of Life in Jewish scripture and interpretation
facts: Genesis places the Tree of Life in Eden alongside the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil.
After the expulsion, Genesis describes concern that humans might eat from the Tree of Life and live forever.
Proverbs uses Tree of Life as a metaphor associated with wisdom.
Later Jewish literature and interpretation develop additional paradise and Tree of Life imagery.
layers.potatoism_reading: This supplies a real textual ancestry for using Tree of Life as a symbol of life, wisdom, mortality and access. Potatoism's tree architecture is a later project synthesis, not an ancient Jewish doctrine.
layers.source: Jewish Encyclopedia, Tree of Life; Genesis 2–3; Proverbs 3

layers.title: Norse world-tree
facts: Yggdrasil is the world-tree described in Old Norse mythological sources, especially the Poetic Edda and Prose Edda.
It is associated with multiple realms and beings and functions as a cosmic organizing image.
The surviving texts are medieval witnesses to traditions whose chronology and development are earlier and complex.
layers.potatoism_reading: Yggdrasil provides a legitimate comparative example of tree-plus-cosmos architecture. Similarity does not establish that Potatoism descends historically from Norse religion.

layers.title: Door/gate and the Son in Christianity
facts: The Gospel of John contains the 'I am the door/gate' saying in John 10, within a discourse using shepherd and sheep imagery.
Christian theology connects Jesus with Son, Word, incarnation, death and resurrection in different doctrinal traditions.
The New Testament's gate/door imagery occurs in more than one context and should not be collapsed into a single technical doctrine.
layers.potatoism_reading: Potatoism deliberately reuses the Door/Son/threshold motif. The project should identify this as Christian reception and symbolic synthesis, not claim that the full Potato architecture is contained in the New Testament.

layers.title: The real thalamus
facts: The thalamus is a paired gray-matter structure in the diencephalon near the center of the brain.
It contains multiple nuclei with sensory, motor, associative, limbic and arousal-related functions.
Many sensory pathways use thalamic nuclei to relay or modulate information toward the cerebral cortex.
The thalamus participates in consciousness, attention, sleep-wake regulation, learning and memory-related circuitry.
layers.potatoism_reading: The project's Father's House/thalamus association can therefore be studied as a metaphor of central relay, filtering and integration. It is not anatomically correct to say that the thalamus literally is a spiritual house or supernatural interface.
sources: NCBI Bookshelf, Major Structures and Functions of the Brain

layers.title: The real pineal gland
facts: The pineal gland is an endocrine structure in the brain that secretes melatonin and participates in circadian timing.
It is not established by neuroscience as a literal spiritual doorway or fifth-dimensional organ.
layers.potatoism_reading: The project's Door/pineal association should remain explicitly metaphorical. The useful research question is why cultures and modern esoteric traditions have repeatedly treated a small central brain structure as a symbol of inner perception.

layers.title: Dimensions and the Potatoism dimensional metaphor
facts: In mathematics and physics, dimensionality describes the number and structure of independent coordinates needed to specify a state or position in a space.
Modern string-theory families use higher-dimensional mathematical frameworks, but this does not establish a spiritual hierarchy of 1D Hell, 2D Frame, 3D Box, 4D society and 5D Door.
The project's 1D–5D sequence is therefore best treated as an internally coherent symbolic model unless separately supported by physical theory.
layers.potatoism_reading: The dimensional ladder can be valuable as a conceptual map of increasing representational complexity, but must not be presented as established physics.

layers.title: Red and Blue Potato as project archetypes
facts: Red and blue potatoes are real horticultural varieties and color categories, but the Life/Strife meanings assigned to them are project symbolism.
Color symbolism varies strongly between cultures and historical periods.
layers.potatoism_reading: The Red/Blue duality is best modeled as complementary dynamics: emergence/expansion versus memory/contraction, rather than good versus evil.

layers.title: Roots as biological and cultural metaphor
facts: Plant roots anchor plants, absorb water and minerals and interact with surrounding soil and microorganisms.
Human languages routinely use root metaphors for ancestry, origin, belonging and foundational causes.
The Tree of Life metaphor combines biological growth with genealogical and cosmological meaning.
layers.potatoism_reading: This gives the Root concept three separable layers: biological root, ancestral/cultural root and project-spiritual root.

layers.title: Spiral as a real mathematical/natural form
facts: Spirals occur in mathematical models and in many natural growth patterns, although biological spirals are not all instances of one universal law.
A spiral can represent repeated movement with changing scale, distance or orientation.
layers.potatoism_reading: The Potatoism spiral can be formalized as a transformation graph: a system revisits related states while changing scale or orientation.

layers.title: North as orientation
facts: North is a geographic directional reference based on Earth's rotational/geographic coordinate system, with magnetic north differing from geographic north.
Human cultures have independently assigned symbolic meanings to cardinal directions, but those meanings vary by tradition.
layers.potatoism_reading: North of North is therefore a project-defined metaphysical extension of a real navigational direction, not a geographic location.

research_questions: Which Potatoism symbols have direct textual predecessors and which are original project constructions?
Which apparent parallels are historical influence, which are independent analogy, and which are modern reception?
How can the Tree/Ladder/Axis/House/Plane architecture be represented as a formal graph rather than a simple hierarchy?
How should the People/Dweller layer distinguish empirical populations from symbolic inhabitants?
How did potatoes move from Andean Indigenous agriculture into European political economy and global food systems?
How do Christian, Jewish, Norse, Mesopotamian, Egyptian, Hindu, Buddhist and other tree/axis/threshold traditions differ before comparison?
integrity: Real-world evidence and project interpretation are deliberately stored side by side but never merged into one claim.
